title: Layered lavender and vanilla soy candle
subtitle: A two-layer poured jar candle with distinct scent zones
excerpt: A two-pour soy wax jar candle with lavender fragrance oil in the bottom layer and vanilla fragrance oil in the top, each layer allowed to set fully before the next pour so the colour line stays clean. Makes one 200 ml jar candle; cure five to seven days before lighting.
sourceNotes: Layered candle technique: Candlemaking by Betty Oppenheimer (1999, Storey). Key technique: second layer must be poured when first layer has set to a firm skin but is not fully cold, fully cold wax can crack from the heat differential of the second pour. Pour second layer at a lower temperature (55 to 60°C) to reduce the heat shock further.

recipe.batchNotes: Work in pairs if making multiple candles: pour first layer in all jars, then pour second layer while the first is still at the right temperature.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cure for five to seven days before the first burn. The lavender-vanilla combination develops cleanly during the cure with no interaction between the scent zones.
recipe.temperatureNote: Pour the first layer at 65°C. Pour the second layer at 55 to 60°C to reduce heat shock and protect the boundary line.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Two years in a cool, dry cupboard. Keep the lid on between burns to preserve the scent in both layers.

glossaryTerms.definition: The first burn of a jar candle, which sets the melt pool. In a layered candle, the first memory burn typically burns through the top layer only; a second full melt cycle reaches the bottom layer.
The resting period after pouring, during which fragrance oil bonds with the wax. Layered candles benefit from the full seven days, the second layer is poured later and may need the extra time.

content.text: A layered lavender and vanilla candle is a two-pour soy wax jar candle with lavender fragrance in the bottom half and vanilla fragrance in the top, each layer set before the next goes in to keep the colour boundary clean. Makes one 200 ml jar candle;
five to seven days before lighting.

items.prepNote: split roughly 70 g per layer; adjust if your jar proportions differ
7% of bottom layer wax weight; add to first batch at 65°C
7% of top layer wax weight; add to second batch at 65°C; vanilla will discolour the top layer golden-brown during cure, normal
cotton wick for a 60 to 70 mm jar; the wick runs the full height of both layers

content.text: Warm the jar, stick the wick tab to the base, and hold with the centring bar. The wick must remain centred through both pours.

Melt 70 g of soy wax to 75°C, cool to 65°C, stir in the lavender essential oil for 30 seconds, and pour into the jar to the halfway mark. Leave to set fully, the surface should be firm and dry to the touch, typically one to two hours at room temperature.

Melt the remaining 70 g of wax to 75°C, cool to 60°C (slightly lower than the first pour, reducing the heat shock), stir in the vanilla fragrance oil, and pour gently over the set lavender layer. Pour slowly against the jar wall to avoid disturbing the boundary. Leave to set fully.

Trim the wick to 6 mm after 24 hours. Cure for five to seven days before lighting. The vanilla top layer will turn golden-brown during the cure, this is from the vanillin in the fragrance oil reacting with the wax, not a defect.

: burn for three to four hours on the first light until the melt pool reaches the jar edge. The candle burns through the vanilla layer first, then the lavender layer on subsequent burns. Trim the wick to 6 mm before each burn.
Two years in a cool, dry place. Keep the lid on when not in use.
